newsitem.title: USA: Eastman Chemical profits down in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Eastman Chemical profits down in first quarter.

text.p: Eastman Chemical Co. said Tuesday its earnings fell sharply in the first quarter, mainly due to lower prices for its Eastapak packaging plastic.

The manufacturer of chemicals, fibers and plastics said its earnings tumbled to $72 million, or 92 cents per share, in the quarter from $112 million, or $1.39 per share in the year-ago period. Sales fell 7 percent to $1.17 billion from $1.26 billion.

"Worldwide increases in industry capacity, along with near-term additional capacity under construction, have created the conditions for the significant price erosion that has occurred for PET bottle resin," said Earnest Deavenport Jr., chairman and chief executive.
"The lower prices do appear to be stimulating new applications, which will likely lead to greater demand."

The Kingsport, Tenn.-based company's Speciality and Performance segment saw operating earnings rise 8 percent from the same quarter a year ago, boosted by strong gains in sales volume of many of its products.
The Chemical Intermediates segment had solid volume growth, but earnings edged lower because of lower selling prices and higher raw material costs, it said.
Eastman Chemical has 17,500 employees in more than 30 countries and had 1996 sales of $4.8 billion. Its stock rose 62.5 cents to $52.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
